mustKnow.title: Execution starts on N2
mustKnow.body: Choose the prisoner during the day. You cannot execute on N1, and executing Town removes your remaining abilities.

goodToKnow.title: A quiet jail night is a lead
goodToKnow.body: No kill while someone is jailed does not prove they are the killer. Jail also has exceptions to its protection and visit blocking.

mustKnow.title: You cannot check the first flip
mustKnow.body: Tribunal delays roles and wills until it ends. Have evidence for the next execution before committing; activating only to prove yourself wastes its value.

goodToKnow.title: Hanging objectives still matter
goodToKnow.body: Tribunal deaths can satisfy Jester or Executioner objectives. Check the setup before relying on the normal two-victim limit.

mustKnow.title: Reveal before you reach trial
mustKnow.body: Reveal when the extra vote changes the outcome. Waiting until you are on trial can leave you unable to use it.

goodToKnow.title: Your vote strength grows
goodToKnow.body: This is not the old fixed-vote model: revealing adds a vote, with further growth on later days while alive. Public identity also exposes you to guessers.

mustKnow.title: Knighthood does not prove loyalty
mustKnow.body: A Knight can be evil. Spend the two charges on evidence, because the extra vote can strengthen the opposing faction.

goodToKnow.title: Defense follows a living Knight
goodToKnow.body: Your Basic Defense depends on a living Knight after knighting resolves. Selecting a future Knight is not protection you already have.

mustKnow.title: Prosecution bypasses the normal trial
mustKnow.body: Use supported evidence, not a demonstration of your role. Prosecuting Town removes your remaining charges.

goodToKnow.title: It counts as a hanging
goodToKnow.body: Jester and Executioner objectives can be fulfilled by Prosecution. You cannot use it during Tribunal, and normally only one Prosecution is allowed per day.

mustKnow.title: Autopsy before a meaningful check
mustKnow.body: Examine compares against collected killer records. Without a suitable autopsy, do not write a meaningful N1 examination.

goodToKnow.title: No match is a limited result
goodToKnow.body: No match means no match to your collected records, not innocent. A Shrouded Town player can also produce killer evidence without voluntary evil action.

mustKnow.title: No Crime does not clear faction
mustKnow.body: Record the exact crimes shown. Town attacks or visits across factions can produce crime; a result is not an automatic guilty verdict.

goodToKnow.title: The two crimes mean different things
goodToKnow.body: Murder concerns an attack that night. Trespassing concerns opposing-faction visiting history. Keep those findings separate in your post.

mustKnow.title: Visitors are not destinations
mustKnow.body: Your report lists visible visitors to the house you watched. It does not tell you where those players went elsewhere or which visitor killed.

goodToKnow.title: Astral visitors stay out of the list
goodToKnow.body: No visible visitors does not rule out astral effects. Avoid exposing protective identities when the observation does not require it.

mustKnow.title: Odd: two Good · even: three Evil
mustKnow.body: Odd-night visions contain at least one Good among two names; even-night visions contain at least one Evil among three. Include your selected target.

goodToKnow.title: At least one does not mean exactly one
goodToKnow.body: The vision gives a group condition. It does not select a single culprit, and framing or concealment can affect the classifications.

mustKnow.title: Friends does not mean two Town
mustKnow.body: Friends is apparent faction compatibility; Enemies is a mismatch. Neither result alone tells you which player is evil.

goodToKnow.title: Your target pool changes
goodToKnow.body: Previously compared and revealed players have targeting restrictions. You normally visit both targets, so keep the exact pair and any failed action in your history.

mustKnow.title: Innocent is not a confirmed ally
mustKnow.body: An Innocent result leaves many evils possible. A Suspicious result can also come from framing; post the literal result before interpreting it.

goodToKnow.title: Some dangerous roles look Innocent
goodToKnow.body: Neutral Killings and the Necronomicon holder can evade a clean guilt check. Combine the result with claims, votes, and other evidence.

mustKnow.title: Bugs persist after placement
mustKnow.body: Separate the night you placed a bug from a later trigger. This role does not provide the old global Coven visit log.

goodToKnow.title: A role report is not a player number
goodToKnow.body: Bug feedback can identify an evil visiting role without naming its owner. No trigger is not universal proof that the target was safe.

mustKnow.title: No visible visit is not no action
mustKnow.body: Report every visible destination. Astral actions can appear as no visit, and visiting a death does not by itself identify the killer.

goodToKnow.title: Extra visits have several explanations
goodToKnow.body: A two-visit result does not prove Seer or Town. Catalyst, changed visibility, and corpse-using abilities can complicate a simple movement deduction.

mustKnow.title: Guard intercepts one harmful visitor
mustKnow.body: You do not grant a normal barrier or stop every attack. A successful interception can kill you, and astral attacks can bypass it.

goodToKnow.title: Protection can preserve the protector
goodToKnow.body: A barrier can save you during the counterattack. Merely guarding someone, or dying for them, does not establish their faction.

mustKnow.title: Check N1 Barrier availability
mustKnow.body: Grace Period prevents Barrier on another player on N1. Record an unavailable action honestly; choosing a target is not evidence you saved them.

goodToKnow.title: Powerful Defense has a ceiling
goodToKnow.body: Unstoppable attacks bypass Barrier. You have one Self Barrier, and your visit can still expose you to a Veteran or rampage.

mustKnow.title: Your attack can kill a friendly visitor
mustKnow.body: Fortify protects the target but attacks one random direct visitor. Avoid joining a crowded protection call without coordination.

goodToKnow.title: It does not attack every visitor
goodToKnow.body: A surviving visitor is not a unique-role identification. Astral visitors avoid retaliation, and defense can explain a failed kill.

mustKnow.title: Choose a role, not a player
mustKnow.body: Aegis protects holders of the chosen Town role. Do not repeat a role on consecutive nights; selecting Oracle itself is available only once.

goodToKnow.title: Tracker and Lookout cannot see Aegis
goodToKnow.body: Aegis is astral: you protect without an ordinary visit for Tracker or Lookout to see. Other players' normal visits remain visible. Aegis can also protect a jailed role holder; record the role selected, not an invented player visit.

mustKnow.title: Build before you place
mustKnow.body: An ordinary N1 is Build, not placement. Keep only one active trap and track dismantling or rebuilding before claiming another placement.

goodToKnow.title: Feedback can outlive the placement night
goodToKnow.body: A later trigger can come from an earlier trap. Report the roles shown without assigning them to player numbers you did not learn.

mustKnow.title: One shot; a miss does not clear
mustKnow.body: Your day shot starts on D2. A miss can reflect Town status or defense and does not publicly demonstrate the ability.

goodToKnow.title: Old suicide advice no longer applies
goodToKnow.body: Do not use the older shoot-Town-and-die rule. Framing and protection can affect eligibility, so choose from evidence rather than using the shot as a test.

mustKnow.title: Absorb first, Unleash later
mustKnow.body: An empty Mirror attempt is not an attack result. Spend the stored attack before trying to Mirror again.

goodToKnow.title: The stored attack keeps its dangers
goodToKnow.body: Unleashing a rampage can hurt allied visitors and use the absorbed role's death label. Unstoppable attacks shatter mirrors rather than supplying a normal absorption.

mustKnow.title: Alert also shoots friendly visitors
mustKnow.body: You have three Alerts. Do not make a protection/Lookout call as the beginner default and then kill the Town players who answer it.

goodToKnow.title: A quiet Alert can still be real
goodToKnow.body: No kills does not disprove Alert. Roleblocks can prevent it, astral visitors bypass it, and protection can keep a direct visitor alive.

mustKnow.title: Load before you shoot
mustKnow.body: Spend a night at home to load before shooting on a later night. You cannot shoot on ordinary N1; shooting Town removes access to the gun.

goodToKnow.title: A failed shot has several explanations
goodToKnow.body: Defense is not the only possible explanation for failure. Control can redirect the shot, and roleblocking can prevent a load.

mustKnow.title: Find the Obsession before Care
mustKnow.body: You cannot use Care before finding your Obsession. The old marriage and proposal templates do not describe this role.

goodToKnow.title: Bestow changes later visit evidence
goodToKnow.body: Day Bestow grants lasting astral visits plus roleblock and control immunity. Later missing visits can reflect that change rather than a false claim.

mustKnow.title: Remember is automatic
mustKnow.body: You do not choose a night remember target. Track the actual transition to an eligible dead Town role instead of inventing a visit.

goodToKnow.title: Keep the role timeline
goodToKnow.body: Town Power has remembering priority. Hidden or altered deaths need not prevent Remember, and multiple Amnesiacs cannot all take the same Unique role.

mustKnow.title: Use a body your role permits
mustKnow.body: A normal Town Retributionist cannot use Stoned bodies or self-protect through a corpse. Do not claim an action from an unsuitable body.

goodToKnow.title: You and the corpse visit differently
goodToKnow.body: You visit the corpse; the corpse visits the destination. Necromancer has corpse-use priority, so a missing action need not mean the original body was invalid.

mustKnow.title: Rejection does not name every visitor
mustKnow.body: Record whether someone was rejected, not identities you did not receive. You cannot Party at the same house on consecutive nights.

goodToKnow.title: An obstacle is not a roleblock
goodToKnow.body: Party rejects uninvited eligible visitors. Astral and Party-immune actions differ, and Poisoner's Smog is not the same mechanic.

mustKnow.title: Hangover prevents a repeat block
mustKnow.body: A successful Drink leaves Hangover. Do not claim a continuous roleblock lock or treat no kill after one block as proof of the killer.

goodToKnow.title: Some targets can retaliate
goodToKnow.body: An uncautious Serial Killer or Full Moon Werewolf can be dangerous to block. Drink does not stop daytime abilities.

mustKnow.title: Check setup and action timing
mustKnow.body: Catalyst is a Unique Outlier and needs a compatible setup. Confirm the current role's Overcharge timing rather than assuming every ability gains an immediate extra use.

goodToKnow.title: Extra actions change movement evidence
goodToKnow.body: Additional visits can be a legitimate Overcharge effect. They do not automatically identify a Seer or another specific role.

mustKnow.title: There is no hidden night result
mustKnow.body: Pilgrim has no active ability. Keep social reads separate from mechanical claims, and check that the setup permits this Outlier.

goodToKnow.title: Votes and records are your contribution
goodToKnow.body: Organize claims and contradictions, ask useful questions, and count votes. Having no night button does not make silence useful.

mustKnow.title: Retrain and book attack compete
mustKnow.body: Do not plan ordinary Retrain and an independent Necronomicon attack on the same night. Role availability and ally retraining have restrictions.

goodToKnow.title: A new role needs a new action history
goodToKnow.body: Retraining changes role, not automatically faction. Recheck your cover's movement and demonstration requirements after a role change.

mustKnow.title: The book changes your movement
mustKnow.body: Book Hex and its Basic Attack become astral. A cover promising a normal visible visit can contradict your real action.

goodToKnow.title: Hex progress is not a completed bomb
goodToKnow.body: Bomb completion has its own trigger and requires the Hex Master to remain active under its conditions. Keep progression private and separate from ordinary attack results.

mustKnow.title: Two targets are not two visits
mustKnow.body: Control normally visits the first player, not both selected numbers. A Seer story is not naturally supported by selecting two targets.

goodToKnow.title: Role knowledge is narrower than a history
goodToKnow.body: Learning a role does not give every result another investigator would see. Immunity, Hangover, charges, and Illumination can limit the next Control or Ritualist follow-up.

mustKnow.title: Night protection is not day protection
mustKnow.body: Check the target's actual daytime defenses before spending the one Meteor. Do not assume last night's barrier still applies.

goodToKnow.title: The cinematic does not name you
goodToKnow.body: The Meteor publicly shows that the ability happened, not which living player used it. A public-reveal Town cover still needs a demonstration you cannot normally give.

mustKnow.title: Check eligibility before guessing
mustKnow.body: Blood Ritual has two attempts. Town Investigatives and Illuminated targets are normally ineligible; a Potion Master reveal is not an immediate guaranteed ritual.

goodToKnow.title: A wrong guess gives no replacement role
goodToKnow.body: Failure spends an attempt without identifying the correct role. Ordinary book attacks and Blood Ritual are alternative actions.

mustKnow.title: A surviving visitor can expose you
mustKnow.body: You attack one non-Coven direct visitor; other direct visitors can learn your identity. A crowded call increases exposure as well as opportunity.

goodToKnow.title: Jinx does not supply a Lookout list
goodToKnow.body: Direct co-visitors can receive a private night message naming you as Jinx and naming the house. The attacked visitor is not a safe exception: if they survive, they can report you too. Your own attack feedback is not a complete visitor list.

mustKnow.title: A cure can prevent Insomnia
mustKnow.body: Dreamwoven Town targets can be cured by a Town visit on the following night. Do not treat every applied status as permanent disruption.

goodToKnow.title: Your continued role matters
goodToKnow.body: Death or retraining of the Dreamweaver normally clears its effects. A cure does not prove the cured player's permanent faction loyalty.

mustKnow.title: Alterate needs the target to die
mustKnow.body: You have two Alterates, and a survivor wastes the use. Coordinate death timing before committing the rewritten role, faction, and will.

goodToKnow.title: Framing cannot rewrite every observation
goodToKnow.body: Do not expect Enchant to manufacture movement that observers directly verify. Coroner, Tracker, Lookout, and Spy resist this kind of information alteration.

mustKnow.title: Illusion is astral; book attacks are direct
mustKnow.body: Your ordinary book attack replaces the protection choice. Changing action mode can break a cover based on having no visible visit.

goodToKnow.title: Appearance is not permanent allegiance
goodToKnow.body: Illusion does not fool every ability, and Reap can override it. Disguise changes shown death information, so graveyard role counts can mislead.

mustKnow.title: Stone is a visible visit, even without a kill
mustKnow.body: Stone is non-harmful, so it can still be available while protection is disabled. If keeping a TP cover during Grace Period, hold N1 instead: an observer can see a visit your claimed protection could not make.

goodToKnow.title: A permanent mark is not protection
goodToKnow.body: Stone hides a marked player's role and will when they later die. It does not protect or immediately kill them. You have three active charges; there is no need to spend one every night.

mustKnow.title: A Ret cover has a smaller body pool
mustKnow.body: Stoned or evil corpses and self-protection can contradict a normal Town Retributionist claim. Ordinary reanimation and book attack are alternatives.

goodToKnow.title: Corpse-use priority can explain a failure
goodToKnow.body: Necromancer acts ahead of Retributionist for corpse use. Some day-role bodies resolve at an appropriate later transition rather than as an ordinary night ability.

mustKnow.title: Drink and Smog are different stories
mustKnow.body: Drink roleblocks; Smog obstructs visits to a house. A Tavern Keeper cover fits ordinary Drink, not an invented repeat block through Hangover.

goodToKnow.title: The book constrains the choice
goodToKnow.body: A direct book attack also roleblocks but cannot normally accompany Smog. Recheck your cover when changing from Drink to a different action mode.

mustKnow.title: Choose one potion mode
mustKnow.body: Barrier, Reveal, and a book-enabled Harmful Potion are choices. Do not claim you healed, revealed, and attacked at once.

goodToKnow.title: Reveal does not grant every result
goodToKnow.body: Role knowledge does not supply actions, crimes, or a Seer's two-visit pattern. Reveal also applies Illumination, which restricts Ritualist follow-up.

mustKnow.title: Changing dolls does not reset targeting
mustKnow.body: You cannot target the same player on consecutive nights, even with a different doll. Plan the next target before choosing Silence, Deafen, or Blind.

goodToKnow.title: Missing feedback is not failed action
goodToKnow.body: Blindness and daytime communication effects do different jobs. A silenced player's lack of a public claim is not voluntary refusal.

mustKnow.title: Keep the two directions separate
mustKnow.body: Sense supplies destinations and visitors, but Tracker reports only destinations and Lookout only visitors. Whispers are not a result either cover receives.

goodToKnow.title: The book ties your attack to Sense
goodToKnow.body: Book attacks retain Sense but attack that same target. Astral actions evade Sense, so your movement information is not exhaustive.

mustKnow.title: No special ability does not mean no obligations
mustKnow.body: Your cover still needs plausible actions and demonstrations. Check that the setup allows this Outlier, and coordinate with Coven rather than inventing a natural ability.

goodToKnow.title: Receiving the book changes the story
goodToKnow.body: A quiet no-visit cover may stop fitting once you make direct book attacks. Teammate information can support a story but cannot create its promised public ability.

mustKnow.title: Conversion changes faction, not the role
mustKnow.body: Your one day Indoctrinate can turn eligible Town into your faction while retaining their ability. Prior Town confirmation no longer establishes current loyalty.

goodToKnow.title: Converted allies are not ordinary Town Traitors
goodToKnow.body: Converted players can receive the Necronomicon. Recheck faction assumptions and book coordination after conversion.

mustKnow.title: Count other living Bread holders
mustKnow.body: Your starting Bread is not an ordinary recipient, and dead recipients do not count toward the normal transformation threshold. Prefer players likely to survive.

goodToKnow.title: Transformation changes your job
goodToKnow.body: After becoming Famine, use the transformed plan rather than feeding again. The public transformation announcement does not identify which player transformed.

mustKnow.title: No N1 attack; kills drive progression
mustKnow.body: Begin attacking after N1. Selecting a victim is not a kill: confirm each upgrade before using the stronger attack or Rampage rules.

goodToKnow.title: Rampage changes collateral risk
goodToKnow.body: The second kill adds Rampage and the third enables War. Once upgraded, account for visitors as well as the selected house.

mustKnow.title: Infection is not a clean visitor log
mustKnow.body: Starting neighbor infections are not N1 visitors. Repeated contact with an already infected player need not create a fresh event.

goodToKnow.title: Switch plans when Pestilence arrives
goodToKnow.body: Infect all living opponents to transform, then use the stack-based Pestilence plan. Astral contact normally does not spread infection.

mustKnow.title: Reap does not kill the target
mustKnow.body: Reap is astral, frames the target, and supplies extra souls when they die. Do not count an attempted Reap as a kill or a normal visit.

goodToKnow.title: Death makes daytime survival urgent
goodToKnow.body: Seven souls transform you into Death. At that point surviving the public day matters more than continuing the earlier soul-collection plan.

mustKnow.title: All three guesses must be right
mustKnow.body: Guess from N2 and respect target restrictions, including TI immunity. A failed set does not tell you which guess was wrong.

goodToKnow.title: Winning precedes the delayed deaths
goodToKnow.body: Correct guesses Doom the victims for later death; their eventual deaths are not required to count the win. Exact Outlier eligibility remains disputed in the reviewed sources.

mustKnow.title: Your target must be hanged while you live
mustKnow.body: A night kill or ordinary day shot is not your win. Keep the assigned target and your own survival central to the plan.

goodToKnow.title: A transition changes the requirements
goodToKnow.body: Prosecution or Tribunal can satisfy the hanging objective. If another death turns you into Jester, follow Jester's participation requirement.

mustKnow.title: Meet Chatterbox and get hanged
mustKnow.body: Suspicion alone is not enough. Complete the daily text participation requirement; whispers, Last Words, and being shot do not substitute for it.

goodToKnow.title: The hanging route affects revenge
goodToKnow.body: Normal trials, Prosecution, and Tribunal have different revenge eligibility. Early Neutral Evil defense also expires; do not plan around it lasting forever.

mustKnow.title: Scour first; no ordinary N1 Plunder
mustKnow.body: This role no longer uses the old duel minigame. A non-Landlubber kill removes your remaining Plunders, so identify targets before spending them.

goodToKnow.title: Other deaths can advance your objective
goodToKnow.body: Survive until all three Landlubbers die. Their identity belongs to the player, so a role change need not remove them from your target list.

mustKnow.title: Check your own gasoline before Ignite
mustKnow.body: Track direct douses, passive visitor douses, and your self-doused state separately. Taking no action can clean you; do not forget this before burning.

goodToKnow.title: Passive douses concern visitors to you
goodToKnow.body: They do not form a Lookout report on another house. Astral visitors avoid passive dousing, and same-night fresh visitors are not guaranteed immediate burns.

mustKnow.title: Choose Cautious deliberately
mustKnow.body: Cautious suppresses retaliation against disruptors. Ordinary roleblocking does not simply stop your role, so align that setting with the cover you are maintaining.

goodToKnow.title: An attack is not guaranteed progression
goodToKnow.body: Target defense can reset Bloodlust progress. Track confirmed outcomes before planning a Powerful Rampage; exact retaliation interactions stay in the deeper rules.

mustKnow.title: The Shrouded target may not visit
mustKnow.body: If the selected player makes no direct visit, the fallback attacks that player. Do not assume every Shroud action is invisible or hits someone else.

goodToKnow.title: A harmful visitor may be innocent
goodToKnow.body: Shroud can make a Town player's direct visit carry an attack and trigger guards or traps. A death gives only limited movement information.

mustKnow.title: Use the actual Full Moon indicator
mustKnow.body: Scent nights and Rampage nights do different jobs. Do not follow an assumed moon schedule or forget danger to visitors when staying home.

goodToKnow.title: Scent reports can persist without a new visit
goodToKnow.body: An old scent can keep returning destinations. A fresh Tracker story about that player can conflict with your real attack elsewhere.

mustKnow.title: Soul Swap does not swap faction
mustKnow.body: After a successful swap, update the actual role and available actions. Your old role's template and the old faction-stealing objective do not apply.

goodToKnow.title: The objective follows the faction profile
goodToKnow.body: Default Wandering Souls seeks to eliminate every Cursed Soul role while a faction member survives. An old known role is not proof of a player's current role.

mustKnow.title: A real Town ability can belong to your faction
mustKnow.body: Conversion retains the target's role while changing allegiance. Do not apply static Town-confirmation logic after a conversion.

goodToKnow.title: Killing Vampire may not end the faction
goodToKnow.body: Converted teammates can inherit Vampire. Defended or non-Town targets do not automatically convert, and the old youngest-biter system does not apply.

famine.dawn: Record your Starve target, actual Bread changes and reported starvation deaths. Recount living opponents and their votes; do not continue a Baker Feed checklist.

mustKnow.title: You are using Starve now
mustKnow.body: Stop following Baker's Feed opening. Target a living opponent with Bread to accelerate its loss, and plan to survive the vote.

goodToKnow.title: Bread delays starvation
goodToKnow.body: Transformation starts the starvation process; it does not instantly eliminate every opponent. Invincible Defense does not prevent hanging.

war.dawn: Record both chosen Rampage targets and the deaths actually shown. Recount surviving votes before deciding your next two targets; an attempted attack is not a confirmed kill.

mustKnow.title: Use the transformed two-target plan
mustKnow.body: War can select up to two useful distinct Rampage targets with Unstoppable attacks. Do not fall back to Berserker's one-target buildup.

goodToKnow.title: Your main remaining danger is the vote
goodToKnow.body: Invincible Defense does not prevent hanging. Count surviving votes while choosing attacks instead of treating transformation as an automatic win.

pestilence.dawn: Record your actual Spread Pestilence action, reported stacks and deaths. Keep this stack-based state separate from the earlier Plaguebearer infection history.

mustKnow.title: Pestilence uses stacks, not the old rampage
mustKnow.body: Use Spread Pestilence rather than continuing the Plaguebearer infection checklist. Three stacks are lethal while the effect is active.

goodToKnow.title: Spread is not a conventional harmful attack
goodToKnow.body: Its action can force maximum stacks. Keep that mechanic separate from the old Town of Salem 1 passive-rampage model and reassess your cover.

death.dawn: After the public transformation, count who can vote against you and answer the current accusations. Surviving this day is the immediate objective; do not plan another Reap.

mustKnow.title: Survive this day
mustKnow.body: After the public transformation, daytime survival is the urgent decision. Do not keep following Soul Collector's night progression plan.

goodToKnow.title: The Apocalypse resolves at the end of day
goodToKnow.body: Vote pressure is the central threat. Keep the cover consistent and private soul counts out of your public will.
